function.description: Read a file from the workspace. `path` is relative to the workspace root. Returns the file's content. If the file is larger than the result limit, the call returns an error stating the file's size; call again with `offset` and `limit` to read part of it. Paths outside the workspace, symbolic links and files the operator has protected are refused.
function.name: read_file

limit.description: Maximum number of bytes to return. Default: to the end of the file.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading at. Default 0.

path.description: Path of the file, relative to the workspace root.

function.description: List a directory in the workspace. `path` is relative to the workspace root; use `.` for the root itself. Returns the names of the entries directly inside it and marks which are directories. It does not descend into subdirectories.
function.name: list_dir

path.description: Path of the directory, relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Search the text of files in the workspace. `pattern` is a regular expression in RE2 syntax, matched against each line. `path`, if given, limits the search to that file or to that directory and everything under it; the default is the whole workspace. Returns the matching lines with their file paths and line numbers. Files the operator has protected are skipped.
function.name: search_files

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default: the whole workspace.

pattern.description: Regular expression in RE2 syntax, matched against each line.

function.description: Fetch a public web page or document with an HTTP GET request. `url` must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL. Returns the response body. The request is checked before it is sent and may be refused; a refusal is returned as an error that gives the reason. A redirect to a different host is not followed: its target is returned so that you can decide whether to fetch it. Do not put workspace content, secrets or personal data in the URL.
function.name: web_fetch

url.description: Absolute http or https URL to fetch.

function.description: Search the web. Returns a list of results, each with a title, a URL and a short extract. The query is checked before it is sent and may be refused; a refusal is returned as an error that gives the reason. Do not put workspace content, secrets or personal data in the query.
function.name: web_search

function.description: Propose creating a file, or replacing the whole content of an existing file. `path` is relative to the workspace root and `content` is the complete new content. Nothing is written to the workspace now: the change is staged, shown to the reviewers as a diff alongside your answer, and applied only if the user chooses to apply it. Reading the path later in this turn returns the staged content.
function.name: write_file

content.description: The complete new content of the file.

path.description: Path of the file, relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Propose replacing one piece of text in a file. `old` must match exactly one place in the file's current content, which is its staged content if you have already changed it in this turn; `new` replaces it. If `old` does not match, or matches more than one place, the call returns an error and nothing changes. The change is staged in the same way as `write_file`: nothing is written to the workspace now.
function.name: edit_file

new.description: The text to put in its place.

old.description: The exact text to replace. It must occur exactly once in the file.

path.description: Path of the file, relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Withdraw your staged change to a path. The path then reads as it did before you changed it, and it is left out of the proposed changes. Use it to retract a file you proposed creating or changing.
function.name: unstage

path.description: Path whose staged change to withdraw, relative to the workspace root.

function.description: Run a shell command and return its output. The command runs with `bash -c` in a private copy of the workspace that includes the changes you have staged in this turn. Standard input is empty and there is no terminal, so the command must not wait for input. Standard output and standard error are returned together, in the order written. Anything the command writes to files is discarded when it ends and does not change the workspace or your staged changes: to propose a change, use `write_file` or `edit_file`. Each command starts from a fresh copy, so nothing carries over from one command to the next; do related steps in one command. The command is checked before it runs and may be refused; a refusal is returned as an error that gives the reason. A command that exits with a non-zero status is returned as a result with its exit code, not as an error. Output beyond the size limit is cut off and the result says so. There is no network access unless the operator has allowed specific hosts.
function.name: bash

command.description: The command line to run with bash -c.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to allow before the command is stopped. Default 120. A value above the maximum is reduced to the maximum.
